subsystems.name: Descent and access system
subsystems.role: safely lowers a robot through a skylight or pit into the void, and may climb back out.
parts: tether and winch or autonomous rappelling legs

subsystems.name: Mobility platform
subsystems.role: traverses rough cave floors, walls and rubble in complete darkness.

subsystems.name: Power system
subsystems.role: provides energy where sunlight never reaches.

subsystems.name: Communication relay
subsystems.role: links the cave robot to the surface and then to Earth through kilometres of rock.

subsystems.name: Science payload
subsystems.role: searches for organic molecules, ices and signs of life.

buildSteps.title: Survey from orbit
buildSteps.detail: High-resolution cameras and radar find cave entrances (skylights) and estimate their size, depth and stability.

buildSteps.title: Test in analog lava tubes
buildSteps.detail: Prototype robots practice descent, communication and sampling in terrestrial lava tubes on Earth.

buildSteps.title: Design the descent system
buildSteps.detail: Choose between a tether from a surface winch or an autonomous rappelling robot that can climb back out.

buildSteps.title: Engineer the communication relay
buildSteps.detail: Deploy a mesh of radio nodes or a fibre-optic cable from the entrance to maintain contact with the robot.

buildSteps.title: Integrate science instruments
buildSteps.detail: Mount spectrometers, drills and sample containers, and test them on cave-analog materials.

buildSteps.title: Launch and land
buildSteps.detail: Deliver the robot and relay to the planetary surface near a cave entrance.

buildSteps.title: Deploy and descend
buildSteps.detail: The robot moves to the skylight, anchors, and lowers itself into the void.

buildSteps.title: Explore and sample
buildSteps.detail: Map the cave with lidar, identify targets, and collect samples of wall coatings, floor dust and ice.

buildSteps.title: Transmit data and return samples
buildSteps.detail: Send science data to Earth; if a sample return is planned, launch samples back.

prerequisites.why: cameras such as HiRISE on Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter and LRO have already spotted skylights and pits.

prerequisites.tech: Autonomous navigation in darkness and without GPS
prerequisites.why: lidar-based mapping works in terrestrial caves, but no robot has done it on another planet.
low-frequency radio and relay chains have been tested in caves on Earth, but not through planetary rock.
RTGs are proven on spacecraft, but miniaturising them for small cave robots remains a challenge.
Raman spectrometers and drills exist for rovers, but not yet packaged for cave environments.
no mission has ever returned samples from a planetary cave.

pathway.milestone: orbital identification of cave candidates on Mars and the Moon, plus terrestrial analog missions
pathway.unlocks: a shortlist of safe, scientifically promising cave entrances.

pathway.milestone: robotic precursor to a lunar pit demonstrating descent, communication and mapping
pathway.unlocks: proven hardware and operations for deeper exploration.

pathway.milestone: Mars cave mission with an astrobiology payload
pathway.unlocks: the first direct search for organic molecules and ice in a shielded subsurface environment.

pathway.milestone: subsurface sample return and human exploration using caves as shelters
pathway.unlocks: definitive answers on past or present life, and safe habitats for astronauts.
